meta.title: IGN 26 — the Indonesian desktop, rebuilt from the ground up
meta.description: IGN 26 ships BAYU, a Wayland desktop where GTK 4 and Qt 6 look the same. Install Linux apps with Flatpak, run Android apps with Lapis, and manage both from Bayu Store. Download the live ISO.

hero.badge: IGN 26 BETA 6 · Live ISO · Bayu desktop built in
hero.h1: The Indonesian desktop, rebuilt from the ground up.
hero.sub: IGN 26 ships BAYU — a Wayland desktop environment where GTK 4 and Qt 6 finally look the same. Install Linux apps with Flatpak, run Android apps with Lapis, and manage both from one store.

bayu.title: One desktop. Two toolkits. No seams.
bayu.body: BAYU is the Wayland desktop environment at the centre of IGN 26, built component by component — compositor, shell, session, file manager, settings and terminal — so that every window shares one visual language instead of three. In the nightly image you can also choose the layout: a Dock with a top bar for the menus, or one Panel along the bottom. Settings > Desktop switches between them at once.

shots.alt: The Dock layout: a top bar with the menus of the app in front, and the dock
The Panel layout: one bar along the bottom, with each app's menus in its window

components.title: Compositor & shell
components.body: A Wayland compositor with its own panel, dock, launcher and overview — no GNOME or KDE shell underneath.

components.title: Session & display manager
components.body: A matching greeter and session manager, so the look starts at the login screen and never breaks.

components.title: File manager
components.body: Tabs, split view, archive handling and Flatpak-aware Open With, in the same window chrome as everything else.

components.title: Settings
components.body: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, display, sound, keyboard, dock and appearance in one searchable app.

components.title: Terminal
components.body: Themed to follow the system accent and light/dark mode automatically.

components.title: Bayu Store
components.body: Flathub and F-Droid in a single catalogue — install, update and remove from one place.

components.title: Nabau installer
components.body: A guided, eight-step installer that works for any systemd Linux distribution.

components.title: Lapis runtime
components.body: Android apps as real Wayland windows, powered by a kernel with binder support.

wallpaper.title: A wallpaper that follows the day
wallpaper.body: The default wallpaper is a set of four pictures of Mount Bromo: morning, day, evening and night. It changes by itself with sunrise and sunset in your time zone, so WIB, WITA and WIT each change at their own times. You can make it follow light and dark mode instead. A second set, a forest, is in Settings > Wallpaper.

phases.name: Morning
phases.when: From half an hour before sunrise

phases.name: Night
phases.when: From half an hour after sunset

pitaloka.title: One source of truth for GTK 4 and Qt 6.
pitaloka.body: Every colour, radius, font step and elevation in BAYU comes from one file: tokens.json. From it, Pitaloka generates a stylesheet for each toolkit, so a GTK 4 app and a Qt 6 app sitting side by side are pixel-consistent — same card radius, same accent, same focus ring.

themes.alt: Bayu Store Discover page in the light theme

themes.name: Dark

pitaloka.caption: The same Bayu Store window in both themes. Nothing is re-drawn — the tokens simply resolve to their dark values, and every GTK and Qt app on the system follows along.

store.title: Flathub and F-Droid, in one catalogue.
store.body: Bayu Store searches Linux and Android sources at the same time and shows the results in one list. Install a Flatpak desktop app and an F-Droid Android app from the same screen, then keep both updated from the same Updates tab.

hero_shot.alt: Bayu Store's Discover page, with apps from Flathub and F-Droid

details.alt: Firefox's page in Bayu Store, with screenshots, licence, size and source
details.caption: App pages with screenshots, release notes, licence and download size — for Flatpak and Android apps alike.

details.alt: The Library tab in Bayu Store listing installed apps
details.caption: One Library tab for everything installed, with version, source and size, plus a single Check for updates.

features.title: Search both worlds at once
features.body: One query returns Flathub and F-Droid results together, ranked and de-duplicated, in well under a second.

features.title: Trust signals up front
features.body: Verified and Open source badges, publisher name, licence and SPDX identifier are shown before you install.

features.title: Filter by what matters
features.body: Narrow by source, licence, verification or recency without leaving the result list.

features.title: Install without a terminal
features.body: One button per app. Progress is inline, and the app lands in the launcher when it finishes.

features.title: Updates in one place
features.body: Flatpak and Android updates share the same queue, with sizes and release notes before you commit.

features.title: Sources you control
features.body: Enable or disable Flathub and F-Droid, add mirrors, and choose how often the catalogue refreshes.

lapis.title: Android apps as ordinary Wayland windows.
lapis.body: Lapis boots a LineageOS-based Android image inside a systemd-nspawn container running on your own kernel. No virtual machine, no LXC, no Python — a single static Go binary and a handful of systemd units. Each Android app opens as its own window, alongside your Linux apps, in the same dock and the same alt-tab.
checks: Google Play, with optional ARM translation
GPU acceleration through host render nodes (Mesa)
Audio routed over PipeWire or PulseAudio
Clipboard sync, notifications and desktop menu entries
Automatic freeze on suspend, so nothing drains in the background
Phone and tablet UI layouts with adjustable window sizes

layers.title: Android apps
layers.body: Each app is a separate Wayland window

layers.title: Lapis · single static Go binary
layers.body: Pure-Go binder · nftables NAT over netlink · DHCP + DNS forwarder · raw BPF seccomp · minimal PID-1 shim

layers.title: Host kernel with binder support
layers.body: Your kernel. No hypervisor, no second scheduler.

nabau.title: An installer any Linux distribution can ship.
nabau.body: Nabau is the guided installer introduced with IGN 26, and it is deliberately distribution-agnostic. Eight plain-language steps, a full review before a single byte is written, GPG-verified packages and Secure Boot support — nothing in the flow is tied to IGOS Nusantara.

featured.alt: Nabau step 5, choosing a base environment and add-ons
featured.caption: Step 05 — pick a base environment, then add only what you need. Package count, download size, installed size and estimated time update as you choose.

steps.title: Language
steps.body: Pick an interface language from twelve

steps.title: Network
steps.body: Wired or Wi-Fi, host name, optional

steps.title: Review
steps.body: Everything on one screen before writing

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Progress, logs and a clean restart

guarantees.title: GPG-verified packages
guarantees.body: Secure Boot stays on, and every package is checked before it lands on disk.

guarantees.title: Your data is kept
guarantees.body: Only the space you choose on the destination is touched. Everything else is left alone.

guarantees.title: Escape hatches
guarantees.body: F1 opens help, F12 drops to a console. The installer never hides what it is doing.

guarantees.title: Twelve languages
guarantees.body: Indonesian, Javanese, Sundanese, Malay, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Russian.

more.title: The parts you only notice when they are missing.

items.title: Twelve interface languages
items.body: Indonesian, Javanese, Sundanese, Malay, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese and Russian — translated across the shell, settings, store and installer.

items.title: Apple hardware support
items.body: Keyboard and trackpad quirks, SMC drivers and sensible Command-key defaults, so a MacBook behaves like a MacBook.

items.title: Wi-Fi out of the box
items.body: Drivers for the Broadcom chipsets in older MacBooks, are on the ISO. The nightly image adds common Realtek, MediaTek, Ralink and Atheros USB adapters. No cable needed to get online during install.

items.title: Built entirely in containers
items.body: Every package and image is produced with Podman in CI, so a build is reproducible and auditable from the first commit.

items.title: Live ISO, no install required
items.body: Boot the image from a USB stick and use the finished system straight away. Install to disk later from the same session — or never, and keep running it live.

items.title: GPL-3.0 and BSD-3-Clause
items.body: Dual-licensed GPL-3.0 and BSD-3-Clause. Every component is free software, with the full source and build recipe published. Nothing is hidden.

items.title: Printers found by themselves
items.body: Network printers and driverless USB printers are set up as soon as they appear. Settings > Printers prints a test page, sets the default and shows the jobs. Scanners work too. In the nightly image now.

items.title: Updates at a restart
items.body: Settings > System Update downloads the system's updates in the background and installs them when you restart. App updates are in Bayu Store. In the nightly image now.

items.title: Hardware tools included
items.body: lsusb, lspci, lshw, hwinfo, sensors, smartctl, nvme, iw and ethtool are there, so you can see what hardware you have and report a problem. In the nightly image now.

download.title: Get IGN 26.
download.sub: Write it to a USB stick and boot. The live session is the finished system — Nabau simply copies it to disk when you are ready.
download.name: IGN 26 · Bayu Live
download.body: The complete Bayu desktop with Bayu Store, Lapis and the Nabau installer. Boot it, try it, and install to disk from the same session. The main download is IGN 26 Beta 6. The nightly image is built from the newest code every day.
download.nightly_note: Nightly has the newest changes, and may have new bugs.
download.host_note: r2.igos-nusantara.or.id · direct download, no mirror selection
cmds: sudo dd if=ign26-bayu-beta6.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress oflag=sync
download.cmd_note: Replace /dev/sdX with your USB device — dd will not ask twice.
